_strings.@@08d58be10593: 2025 Utah TC-40 Individual Income Tax Instructions, "When to File and Pay" — "You must file your return and pay any tax due... by April 15, 2026, if you file on a calendar year basis (tax year ends Dec. 31, 2025)"; fiscal-year filers use the 15th day of the fourth month after year end; a weekend/legal-holiday due date moves to the next business day; the due date may change if the IRS changes the federal due date
_strings.@@09b584b300aa: Taxpayer Tax Credit — Available to essentially all Utah resident filers (and apportioned for part-year/nonresidents). It is the broad general credit that offsets Utah's flat 4.5% income tax. The credit is reduced (phased out) as income rises above a base amount tied to filing status, and reaches zero for higher earners. Filers whose federal AGI is less than their federal standard deduction are instead "qualified exempt taxpayers" and owe no Utah tax (TC-40 line 21).
_strings.@@1a4597951262: Utah Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC) — You must (1) qualify for and claim the federal earned income tax credit in the same tax year, and (2) earn Utah income that is reported on a federal W-2. The credit is limited to the amount of Utah wages (Earned Income Tax Credit Worksheet: enter the LESSER of 20% of the federal credit or total Utah W-2 box 16 wages). Nonrefundable: it can reduce Utah income tax to zero but any excess is not refunded and cannot be carried forward or back.

_strings.@@48f49d891a0e: Treaty conformity — UT conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from UT income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the UT return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: Utah's resident return (TC-40) starts from federal adjusted gross income (FAGI). 2025 TC-40 Line 4 is "Federal adjusted gross income from federal return." Federally treaty-exempt income is already excluded from FAGI and flows through. The full list of 2025 TC-40A Part 1 "Codes for Additions to Income" — 51 (lump sum distribution), 53 (medical care savings account addback), 54 (my529 addback), 56 (child's income excluded from parent's return), 57 (municipal bond interest), 60 (untaxed income of a resident trust), 61 (untaxed income of a nonresident trust), 67 (tax paid on behalf of a pass-through entity taxpayer), 68 (Payroll Protection Program grant or loan addback), 69 (equitable adjustments) — contains NO add-back of income exempt under a federal tax treaty (the code list is unchanged from 2024 and 2023). The instructions' "Income from Other Countries" section reinforces this: "Utah residents who live and work abroad must pay Utah tax on income earned in other countries if the income is included in federal adjusted gross income on the federal return. There is no Utah credit for taxes paid to another country." The "Foreign Nationals & Expatriates" section adds that a foreign national or expatriate who meets Utah domicile is a resident and "must pay tax on income earned from Utah sources if that income is included in your adjusted gross income on your federal return." Therefore treaty-exempt income is NOT re-taxed by Utah -> conforms = true.

If the result is zero or less, enter 0'; Line 11 'The Utah personal exemption is $2,111 per dependent'; the Line 17 table ($18,213 Single / $36,426 Married filing jointly / $18,213 Married filing separately / $27,320 Head of household / $36,426 Qualifying surviving spouse); 'Rounding Off to Whole Dollars: Round off cents to the nearest whole dollar. _strings.@@85f3d0421fdb: At-Home Parent Credit — An at-home parent (biological mother/father, stepmother/stepfather, adoptive parents, foster parents, legal guardian, or a person housing a child placed by a child-placing agency for legal adoption) who provides full-time care in their residence for a child 12 months old or younger on the last day of 2025, with the child claimed as a dependent on the at-home parent's return. The at-home parent's total W-2 wages/tips/compensation plus federal Schedule C line 7 gross income must be $3,000 or less for the tax year, and federal adjusted gross income (TC-40 line 4) must be $50,000 or less. Nonrefundable; no carryforward/back.
_strings.@@b9dd3adf270a: Utah Child Tax Credit (age window EXPANDED for 2025) — Available for each child who (1) qualifies for the federal child tax credit under IRC 24, and (2) was, on the last day of 2025, NO MORE THAN FIVE YEARS OLD. HB 106 (2025) expanded the window — for 2024 the child had to be at least one and no more than three years old. Phased out by modified adjusted gross income. Nonrefundable; no carryforward/back.

They come with a five-year recapture schedule that this pack does not transcribe (see `unverified`), and this pack's `credits` list does not carry them. _strings.@@f0ca5229d698: Retirement Credit — You (and/or your spouse, if filing jointly) must have been born on or before Dec. 31, 1952. You may NOT claim it if you (or your spouse) claim either the Social Security Benefits Credit (code AH) or the Military Retirement Credit (code AJ). Nonrefundable: reduces tax to zero but no refund of excess; no carryforward/back. Because the maximum is only $450, the instructions note many filers do better with the Social Security Benefits Credit or the Military Retirement Credit.

The $1,000-per-child amount, the 10%-of-excess-MAGI phase-out and its thresholds ($27,000 MFS / 1040NR; $54,000 MFJ and QSS; $43,000 single and head of household) are unchanged from 2024. Tax line: Form TC-40 Line 10: 'Utah tax - multiply line 9 by 4.5% (.045) (not less than zero)' (Line 9 = Utah taxable income/loss = Line 6 total income minus Lines 7-8; Line 4 starts from federal AGI). This op computes the state's flat-rate tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: Rate change for 2025: HB 106 (2025 General Session) lowered Utah's flat individual income tax rate from 4.55% to 4.5% (2025 TC-40 instructions, What's New; the 4.5% rate is printed on Line 10 of the 2025 TC-40 itself). Utah's rate has now moved three years running — 4.65% (2023), 4.55% (2024), 4.5% (2025); never carry it forward. Base guidance: supply 2025 Form TC-40 Line 9 'Utah taxable income/loss' — Line 4 federal adjusted gross income plus Line 5 additions (TC-40A Part 1, codes 51-69) minus Line 7 (state tax refund included on federal Schedule 1) and Line 8 subtractions (TC-40A Part 2). The op multiplies it by 4.5%, producing the Line 10 tax before credits. CRITICAL — Taxpayer Tax Credit (TC-40 Lines 11-20, NOT modeled): Utah has no standard deduction and no base personal exemptions; their function is replaced by a nonrefundable CREDIT against the Line 10 tax. Line 16 initial credit = 6% (.06) of [Line 11 Utah personal exemption ($2,111 x line 2d qualifying dependents — dependents ONLY, not taxpayer/spouse) + Line 12 federal standard or itemized deductions - Line 14 state income tax from federal form 1040, Schedule A, line 5e less lines 5b and 5c]. It phases out at 1.3% (.013) of Line 9 income above the Line 17 base: $18,213 single or married filing separately; $27,320 head of household; $36,426 married filing jointly or qualifying surviving spouse (RAISED for 2025 from $17,652/$26,478/$35,304). Line 22 Utah income tax = Line 10 minus Line 20 (not less than zero). This op returns the LINE 10 amount — compute Lines 11-22 on the form. exemptions ships empty and standard_deduction ships null intentionally: the $2,111 personal exemption and the federal standard/itemized deduction are inputs to the Line 20 CREDIT, never subtractions from the Line 9 base — pass exemptions_count=0 and dependents_count=0. (The 2025 form also newly splits line 2 dependents into a = age 16 and under, b = other dependents, c = dependents born in 2025, d = total; only the line 2d total feeds Line 11.) Qualified exempt taxpayer (TC-40 Line 21, NOT modeled): if federal adjusted gross income is LESS THAN the federal standard deduction (excluding the extra age-65/blind amounts), the filer is exempt from Utah income tax entirely — check the Line 21 worksheet before relying on the computed tax. Zero floor: Line 10 prints 'not less than zero' and the instructions say 'If the result is zero or less, enter 0' — a Line 9 loss produces $0 tax (the op clamps a negative base to $0). Rounding (instructions, 'Rounding Off to Whole Dollars'): 'Round off cents to the nearest whole dollar. Round down if under 50 cents; round up if 50 cents and above' — matches this op's whole-dollar half-up rounding exactly. Not modeled — credits and later lines: apportionable nonrefundable credits on Line 24 (TC-40A Part 3 — the 20%-of-federal Utah EITC code AM, the $450/$900 retirement credit code 18, the Social Security benefits credit code AH now at 4.5% with RAISED $45,000/$90,000/$54,000 phase-out thresholds, the $1,000-per-child child tax credit code AT whose age window HB 106 EXPANDED to children five and younger, the 4.5% capital gain / gold-and-silver-coin credits, the 4.5% military retirement credit AJ, and the new employer-provided childcare credits AW/AX), nonapportionable credits (Line 26, e.g. the $100 at-home parent credit code 01), use tax (Line 31) and the TC-40B non/part-year resident apportionment (Line 25) all come after Line 10 on the form.
